steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on maximizing throughput in multi-band optical networks using column generation. Give the background on the move from fixed-grid WDM to flexible and multi-band networks, then state the problem and how our formulation extends prior column generation work.

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
In the past decade, traditional wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) optical networks, which have fixed-grid frequency slots of 50\text{\,}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}, have moved toward flexible optical networks. These benefit from more flexibility when assigning fiber spectrum resources, and they can now allocate frequency slots of variable size at granularities that are multiples of 12.5\text{\,}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}. More recently, multi-band (MB) transmission was proposed to use fiber spectrum resources beyond the C-band, e.g., the L and U-bands. For these bands, the spectrum width, the transmission performance, and the cost of devices are very different. These differences between bands have to be carefully considered when doing the Route and Wavelength Assignment (RWA). Also, because the number of usable wavelengths is increasing in MB optical networks, the complexity of RWA becomes a new concern.

This paper studies the problem of throughput maximization in MB networks, which requires solving the Route, Wavelength, and Band Assignment (RWBA). We formulate RWBA as an integer linear programming (ILP) model, and to deal with its high complexity we propose an approach based on column generation (CG). In this approach, a column is a colorless configuration, which describes how multiple routes are assigned to the same wavelength. Each column can be used repeatedly across the whole spectrum. This formulation had different names in earlier RWA studies, for example independent set and routing configuration, among others. Here we choose wavelength configuration to highlight that it is strictly related to wavelength channel assignments. After the concept of wavelength configuration first appeared in CG in an earlier study, later work studied new and improved formulations, enhancements to the scalability of the algorithm, and an expansion to multicast routing. In this paper, we extend the concept of wavelength configuration in CG to include: (i) flexible transceivers that can modulate the transmission parameters according to the quality of transmission (QoT) of the lightpath, and (ii) MB transmission, taking into account the heterogeneous requirements across optical bands and addressing its inherent scalability issue.

steps.name: cited_draft
steps.text:
In the past decade, traditional wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) optical networks, which have fixed-grid frequency slots of 50\text{\,}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}, have moved toward flexible optical networks. These benefit from more flexibility when assigning fiber spectrum resources, and they can now allocate frequency slots of variable size at granularities that are multiples of 12.5\text{\,}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}. More recently, multi-band (MB) transmission was proposed to use fiber spectrum resources beyond the C-band, e.g., the L and U-bands [1]. For these bands, the spectrum width, the transmission performance, and the cost of devices are very different. These differences between bands have to be carefully considered when doing the Route and Wavelength Assignment (RWA). Also, because the number of usable wavelengths is increasing in MB optical networks, the complexity of RWA becomes a new concern.

This paper studies the problem of throughput maximization in MB networks, which requires solving the Route, Wavelength, and Band Assignment (RWBA). We formulate RWBA as an integer linear programming (ILP) model, and to deal with its high complexity we propose an approach based on column generation (CG). In this approach, a column is a colorless configuration, which describes how multiple routes are assigned to the same wavelength. Each column can be used repeatedly across the whole spectrum. This formulation had different names in earlier RWA studies, for example independent set [2] and routing configuration [3], among others. Here we choose wavelength configuration [4] to highlight that it is strictly related to wavelength channel assignments. After the concept of wavelength configuration first appeared in CG in [3], later work studied new and improved formulations [5], enhancements to the scalability of the algorithm [4], and an expansion to multicast routing [6]. In this paper, we extend the concept of wavelength configuration in CG to include: (i) flexible transceivers that can modulate the transmission parameters according to the quality of transmission (QoT) of the lightpath, and (ii) MB transmission, taking into account the heterogeneous requirements across optical bands and addressing its inherent scalability issue.

References:
[1] N. Sambo et al. , “Provisioning in multi-band optical networks,” IEEE J. Lightw. Technol. , vol. 38, no. 9, pp. 2598–2605, May 2020.
[2] R. Ramaswami et al. , “Routing and wavelength assignment in all-optical networks,” IEEE/ACM Trans. Netw. , vol. 3, no. 5, pp. 489–500, 1995.
[3] T. Lee, K. Lee, and S. Park, “Optimal routing and wavelength assignment in wdm ring networks,” IEEE J. Sel. Area. Comm. , vol. 18, no. 10, pp. 2146–2154, Oct. 2000.
[4] B. Jaumard et al. , “Efficient spectrum utilization in large scale RWA problems,” IEEE/ACM Trans. Netw. , vol. 25, no. 2, pp. 1263–1278, 2017.
[5] B. Jaumard, C. Meyer, and B. Thiongane, “On column generation formulations for the RWA problem,” Discrete Applied Mathematics , vol. 157, no. 6, pp. 1291–1308, 2009.
[6] F. Zhou et al. , “Joint optimization for multicast provisioning in mixed-line-rate optical networks with a column generation approach,” IEEE J. Lightw. Technol. , vol. 36, no. 3, pp. 637–649, Feb. 2018.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
In the past decade, traditional wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) optical networks characterized by fixed-grid frequency slots of 50\text{\,}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z} have moved toward flexible optical networks, which benefit from higher flexibility in assigning fiber spectrum resources and can now allocate variable-size frequency slots at granularities that are multiples of 12.5\text{\,}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}. More recently, multi-band (MB) transmission was proposed to exploit fiber spectrum resources beyond the C-band, e.g., the L and U-bands [1]. Across these bands, the spectrum width, transmission performance, and cost of devices are very different, and these differences should be carefully considered when performing the Route and Wavelength Assignment (RWA). Moreover, due to the increasing number of usable wavelengths in MB optical networks, RWA complexity becomes a new concern.

This paper investigates the problem of throughput maximization in MB networks, which requires solving the Route, Wavelength, and Band Assignment (RWBA). We formulate RWBA as an integer linear programming (ILP) model and address its high complexity with an approach based on column generation (CG). In this approach, a column corresponds to a colorless configuration, describing how multiple routes are assigned to the same wavelength, and each column may be used repeatedly across the whole spectrum. This formulation had different names in prior RWA studies, such as independent set [2] and routing configuration [3], among others. Here we choose wavelength configuration [4] to highlight its strict relation to wavelength channel assignments. After the concept of wavelength configuration first appeared in CG in [3], new and improved formulations [5], enhancements to the algorithm's scalability [4], and an expansion to multicast routing [6] were studied. In this paper, we extend the concept of wavelength configuration in CG to incorporate: (i) flexible transceivers that can modulate the transmission parameters according to the quality of transmission (QoT) of the lightpath, and (ii) MB transmission, considering the heterogeneous requirements across optical bands and addressing its inherent scalability issue.

References:
[1] N. Sambo et al. , “Provisioning in multi-band optical networks,” IEEE J. Lightw. Technol. , vol. 38, no. 9, pp. 2598–2605, May 2020.
[2] R. Ramaswami et al. , “Routing and wavelength assignment in all-optical networks,” IEEE/ACM Trans. Netw. , vol. 3, no. 5, pp. 489–500, 1995.
[3] T. Lee, K. Lee, and S. Park, “Optimal routing and wavelength assignment in wdm ring networks,” IEEE J. Sel. Area. Comm. , vol. 18, no. 10, pp. 2146–2154, Oct. 2000.
[4] B. Jaumard et al. , “Efficient spectrum utilization in large scale RWA problems,” IEEE/ACM Trans. Netw. , vol. 25, no. 2, pp. 1263–1278, 2017.
[5] B. Jaumard, C. Meyer, and B. Thiongane, “On column generation formulations for the RWA problem,” Discrete Applied Mathematics , vol. 157, no. 6, pp. 1291–1308, 2009.
[6] F. Zhou et al. , “Joint optimization for multicast provisioning in mixed-line-rate optical networks with a column generation approach,” IEEE J. Lightw. Technol. , vol. 36, no. 3, pp. 637–649, Feb. 2018.
